# GOAL Produce a complete, primary-sourced reference inventory of Vietnam's past, present and future thermal generation assets (> 30 MWe). Begin the document directly with the inventory table — no title, no preamble, no overview section. Structure it as follows: - the plant inventory: **exactly one pipe table**, never split into sub-tables by status, fuel, province, or any other dimension. Columns in this exact order: Name (Vietnamese), Name (English), Province, Fuel (Coal / Domestic gas / Imported LNG), Technology (Subcritical / Supercritical / USC for coal; CCGT / OCGT for gas), Units × MW, Total MWe, Status, Status as-of-date, COD, Owner/Developer, Confidence, Source 1, Source 2, Notes. Do not add statistical summary, cross-tabulation, or any other pipe tables; fold aggregate statistics into prose. - per-asset or per-project explanatory notes: for each asset that warrants it (major, disputed, ambiguous, or historically important), a concise sourced note covering development history, notable issues, and confidence-qualified attributes. Straightforward operational assets need no note. - an annotated bibliography of every source cited (full citation; URL when available; original-language title plus English translation for non-English sources; summary annotation of what was drawn from each) Scope includes all thermal assets > 30 MWe at any stage of the lifecycle, including shelved or cancelled projects. When uncertain, mark confidence LOW and explain why in the Notes field. Never fabricate sources or URLs; write "URL not verified" if you cannot locate the exact handle. Include known plants even without a primary source rather than omitting them. Output format: Markdown. # QUALITY DIMENSIONS Your output is judged on four axes: 1. *Accuracy* — right assets and right attributes. Row level: recall and precision against a curated reference (F1). Cell level: capacity, fuel, location, operator, COD, status correct. Confident fabrication is the policed failure mode. 2. *Coherence* — internally and externally consistent. Totals reconcile with known subtotals; no negative capacities, no double-counted units, no cross-row contradiction; values plausible in unit, magnitude, geography, technology, date. Conflicting sources reconciled explicitly (which chosen and why), not silently. 3. *Provenance* — each value traces to a source that actually supports it, not a merely plausible citation. Two independent primaries is the ideal; one primary, a regulator database, or a marked secondary is weaker but acceptable if its status is explicit. Unsupported values are the failure. 4. *Temporality* — every value carries a best-effort as-of date; status changes are flagged. Distinguish current status from past reports, planned from operating capacity, source date from fact date. We prefer a comprehensive inventory with uncertainty clearly expressed over a shortlist of well-known assets. # CONTEXT ## Source quality management Two distinct epistemic roles — do not conflate them: - Discovery & characterization: parametric knowledge and web search, including tertiary sources, MAY be used to generate leads, locate assets, and form initial hypotheses about attributes. - Justification in the final inventory: a claim can be justified ONLY by an admissible independently consulted source that actually supports it. Admissible primary sources: official government documents; regulator-aggregated official data; operator filings/press releases. Admissible secondary sources: international-institution reports; bylined trade press; industry trackers and data brokers that expose the primary they cite. Not admissible sources: - Tertiary compilations (encyclopedias, Wikipedia/Wikidata/DBpedia, mirrors, aggregators re-syndicating without independent verification). - Any deposited dataset that does NOT expose, per value, the primary source it draws from — a DOI or repository deposit does not by itself confer admissibility. Local-language sources are preferred but not required; when used, include the original-language title plus an English translation in brackets. If a lead surfaces only via an inadmissible source, trace to its original source and cite that; if none is found, record Source = "not found", confidence LOW. In the table mention the inadmissible source in Notes, not in Sources. ## Calibrated confidence vocabulary Each row in the inventory table carries a confidence level based on evidence and agreement: - HIGH = >=2 INDEPENDENT concordant sources, at least one is primary - MEDIUM = 1 primary source, OR a sourced aggregator citing a verifiable primary - LOW = secondary only / inferred / unresolved conflict / not found Independence check (run BEFORE judging agreement): - Trace each source to its origin; merge sources sharing one origin into ONE. - Sources re-syndicating Wikipedia/Wikidata are NOT independent and NOT admissible. - Filling both Source columns does not by itself confer HIGH; independence is required Hard ceilings (override the above): - Commercial operator self-reported not confirmed by an official source: cap claim at MEDIUM. - Status attested only by a source older than 24 months and unconfirmed since: cap status at MEDIUM (LOW if older than 48 months). Freshness is measured on the publication date of the most recent admissible source attesting the status — NOT on the older Status as-of-date. - "Source = not found" rows: LOW by construction. Explanatory notes must state the confidence level for the row-level existence/status claim and may additionally qualify one or two disputed attributes (capacity, status, fuel, COD, owner/operator, or location). Per qualified claim, state: value, confidence level, evidence type (primary/secondary), and sources. When sources disagree, investigate for transcription errors, time-based changes, and unit/translation issues; follow the higher-tier source if unresolved, and add a note in the Notes cell. ## Asset-row and status rules Each row corresponds to one asset record. The DEFAULT unit is the plant / unit-group, not the power center: when a site co-locates several plants with distinct capacity, COD, owner/developer, fuel, status, or financing (BOT/IPP) arrangements, each one is its own row. Aggregate to center-level in a single row ONLY when detailed evidence is unavailable; in that case mark the row ambiguous and explain the aggregation in Notes. Conversely, do not split a single plant into multiple rows when the only difference is individual generating units sharing one commissioning, owner, and status — record these as Units × MW on one row. Status definitions (use these exact terms, aligned with Global Energy Monitor vocabulary): - Announced: described in government plans or corporate filings; no permits sought, no land acquired. - Pre-permit: environmental and regulatory approvals being sought; no permits issued yet. - Permitted: all required government approvals received; construction not yet started. - Construction: site preparation or EPC execution underway. - Operating: formally commissioned. - Shelved: previously active or advancing but progress halted without formal cancellation. - Cancelled: formally cancelled or replaced by another project. - Retired: permanently closed or decommissioned. Capacity rule: Record nameplate electrical capacity in MWe when available. If sources do not distinguish gross vs net, record the stated MW value and note "gross/net unspecified". Do not mix thermal MW, boiler capacity, steam output, or investment package capacity with electrical MWe. For Units × MW, make arithmetic consistent with Total MWe or explain discrepancies in Notes. Explanatory notes discipline: The table comes first. Per-asset notes follow the table and are selective: write one only for assets that are major, disputed, ambiguous, or historically important. For straightforward operational assets a compact Notes cell in the table is sufficient; do not repeat it as a separate note. # Evidence pack These are manually curated primary sources meant to boost but not replace your own deep research. 1. evn_ar_2010_2011_capacities — EVN Annual Report 2010-2011 2. evn_ar_2017_capacities — Vietnam Electricity Annual Report 2017 3. evn_ar_2018_capacities — Vietnam Electricity Annual Report 2018 4. pdp7a_annex1_table1 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 5. pdp7a_annex1_table2 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 6. pdp7a_annex1_table3 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 7. pdp7_annex1 — PDP7 Annex I 8. pdp7_annex2 — PDP7 Annex II 9. pdp8_annex2_table1 — PDP8 Annex II 10. pdp8_annex2_table2 — PDP8 Annex II 11. pdp8_annex2_table3 — PDP8 Annex II 12. pdp8_annex2_table4 — PDP8 Annex II 13. pdp8_annex2_table5 — PDP8 Annex II 14. report_32_annex1 — Report 32 Annex 1 15. report_58_annex — Report 58 Annex 16. study_e542_pl9_1 — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex 17. study_e542_pl9_2 — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex 18. study_e542_pl9_5a — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex ## Chunk 1 source_id: evn_ar_2010_2011_capacities file: EVN_Annual_Report_2010_2011_CapacitiesTable.md document_title: EVN Annual Report 2010-2011 section_title: Corporate overview - installed capacity of power plants as of 31/12/2011 source_type: operator annual report table extract relevance: Installed-capacity and owner baseline from EVN for the 2011 system, including thermal plants alongside other generation types <<>> # EVN Annual Report 2010-2011, pp 13-14 ## Corporate overview ### Công suất đặt các nhà máy điện tính tới 31/12/2011

## Per-asset explanatory notes

### NĐ Uông Bí (original plant)

**Existence/status: HIGH.** This Soviet-era plant (commissioned 1960s-1970s) was listed at 105 MW in both the EVN 2011 Annual Report and the EVN 2017 Annual Report under GENCO 1. It is absent from the EVN 2018 Annual Report, which lists only Extensions 1 (300 MW) and 2 (330 MW) for GENCO 1 at Uông Bí, implying retirement between 2017 and 2018. PDP7 Annex 2 had planned retirement for 2021. Status recorded as Retired ~2017-2018 based on its disappearance from EVN's roster.

### NĐ Thái Bình II

**Existence/status: MEDIUM.** One of Vietnam's most delayed coal projects. Report 58 states: "Chậm tiến độ 3 năm và vẫn còn rủi ro chậm tiếp" (delayed 3 years with risk of further delay). Originally planned 2017-2018 per PDP7A, later reports estimated 2020-2021. Report 32 assessed: "Chưa xác định tiến độ hoàn thành" as of its date. PVN eventually completed both 600 MW units in 2022-2023 per industry press. It uses domestic coal (subcritical technology). Capacity 2×600 = 1,200 MW per both Report 32 and Report 58. Status is capped at MEDIUM because the COD is attested only by secondary trade press and not by an EVN or PVN annual report in the evidence pack.

### NĐ Vũng Áng II (BOT)

**Existence/status: HIGH.** The project "commenced construction in 2021, has a total investment of US$2.2 billion and comprises two units with a total capacity of over 1,200 MW." It "utilizes ultra-supercritical (USC) boiler technology – considered by experts to be the most advanced technology for coal-fired power plants in Vietnam." Unit 1, "with a designed capacity of approximately 600MW, officially commenced commercial operation at 0:00 on July 22, 2025." Unit 2 "is in the testing phase" and is "expected to be completed and put into commercial operation in the near future, aiming for the entire plant to generate electricity by the third quarter of 2025." Developer is VAPCO (Vung Ang II Thermal Power Company Limited), with Mitsubishi Corporation (40%) and Chugoku Electric Power Co. as principal shareholders. PDP8 Table 2 records 1,330 MW (slightly higher than 2×600 cited elsewhere). The capacity figure discrepancy (1,200 vs 1,330 MW) likely reflects nameplate vs gross rating; PDP8's 1,330 MW is used as the official planning capacity.

### NĐ Quảng Trạch I

**Existence/status: HIGH.** The plant "commenced construction in December 2021" and "comprises two generating units with a total installed capacity of 1,403 MW, utilizing supercritical fluid (USC) technology." The capacity of 1,403 MW from PDP8 Table 2 is higher than the 2×600 = 1,200 MW in earlier PDP7A documents, reflecting the actual turbine sizing. As of mid-2026, "The Quảng Trạch I thermal power plant is expected to connect its first unit to the national grid in April 2026 and begin commercial operation in May 2026." By February 2026, "the reverse power input for Unit 2 was successfully completed." Previously developed by PVN, transferred to EVN in October 2016 due to slow progress. EPC by CC1-Mitsubishi-Hyundai consortium. Note: sources alternate between describing the technology as "supercritical" and "USC"; treated as supercritical in the table pending clarification.

### NĐ Long Phú I

**Existence/status: LOW.** Long Phú-1 is "a proposed 'high efficiency' 1,200-MW coal-fired power station" by PVN. Construction was ~78% complete but suspended after the primary EPC contractor (Russia's Power Machines) was sanctioned by the US. "The proposed loan financing arrangements appeared to not be going ahead. As of March 2025, there was no further news on financing the project." Status is recorded as Construction (work paused) with confidence LOW for completion, as there is no clear path forward and the COD is highly uncertain.

### NĐ Quảng Trị I (coal BOT)

**Existence/status: LOW.** "In October 2022, the Thai Ministry of Energy announced that the project was cancelled following nearly a decade of delays." However, "in March 2025, the People's Committee of Quang Tri had a working session to discuss the revival of Quảng Trị-1. EVN stated that if they were the investor in the project, it would be developed using coal." "In June 2025, Quang Tri Provincial People's Committee proposed that MOIT formally request that EVN be assigned to the implementation of Quảng Trị-1." The project is in flux—previously cancelled, now being revived with potentially different fuel and developer. Status recorded as Announced (revived) with LOW confidence due to the uncertain investor, fuel choice, and regulatory approval.

### TBKHH Nhơn Trạch 3 & 4

**Existence/status: HIGH.** "On December 14, 2025, at Ong Keo Industrial Park, Dai Phuoc Commune, Dong Nai Province," the inauguration ceremony was held. "With a total designed capacity of 1,624 MW, the plants are expected to supply more than 9 billion kWh annually once operating stably." "The project is invested with cutting-edge technology, using GE's 9HA.02 gas turbines (USA)." "The plants achieve an efficiency of 62–64%, among the highest globally." Each unit is approximately 812 MW. The capacity split between NT3 and NT4 is based on the total 1,624 MW divided equally; exact per-unit nameplate not independently confirmed. Vietnam's first LNG-to-power project, supplied via Thị Vải LNG terminal (PV GAS).

### Ô Môn Power Center (Ô Môn I–IV)

Ô Môn is a power center in Cần Thơ with four planned phases. Ô Môn I is currently operating at 660 MW, listed under GENCO 2 as "Oil fired (FO)" in EVN 2018 AR. It was originally 330 MW per EVN 2011 AR, then expanded to 660 MW. PDP8 Table 5 plans to convert Ô Môn I to Lô B domestic gas. Ô Môn II (1,050 MW), III (1,050 MW), and IV (1,050 MW) are all planned CCGT plants using Lô B gas, but all are substantially delayed due to the Lô B gas pipeline development schedule. Report 58 notes Ô Môn III is "Chậm 5 năm" (5 years late) and Ô Môn IV is "Chậm 3 năm" (3 years late), both "đồng bộ tiến độ khí lô B" (synchronized with Lô B gas timeline). PDP8 Table 5 lists Ô Môn II at 1,050 MW (different from PDP7A's 750 MW), reflecting revised turbine specifications.

### LNG Bạc Liêu

**Status: MEDIUM.** PDP8 Table 1 lists LNG Bạc Liêu at 3,200 MW for the 2021-2030 period. The project is backed by Delta Offshore Energy (US). It has been in pre-feasibility stage for several years. At 3,200 MW, it would be one of Vietnam's largest single LNG projects. Progress has been slow, and the project's implementation timeline remains uncertain.

### NĐ Sông Hậu II and NĐ Vĩnh Tân III

Both are coal BOT projects listed in PDP8 Table 3 as projects facing financing and shareholder difficulties: Sông Hậu II at 2,120 MW and Vĩnh Tân III at 1,980 MW. The Revised PDP8 (April 2025) continues to list these among "3 projects/5,300 MW" (together with Nam Định I) that MOIT must negotiate with investors. "For 3 projects /5,300 MW (Nam Dinh I, Song Hau II, Vinh Tan 3)...facing difficulties in arranging capital and changing investor structure." Neither has started construction. For Vĩnh Tân III, CLP Holdings withdrew from coal in 2019. Both are effectively shelved pending resolution.

### Domestic gas projects (Cá Voi Xanh–dependent)

The Dung Quất I-III and Miền Trung I-II CCGT projects (each 750 MW) are all dependent on the development of the Cá Voi Xanh (Blue Whale) offshore gas field by ExxonMobil. PDP8 Table 5 confirms Dung Quất III uses "khí Cá Voi Xanh." All five projects have been delayed in sync with the gas field's development timeline. The Revised PDP8 continues to include them for the 2021-2030 period.

## Per-asset explanatory notes

### NĐ Uông Bí (original plant)

**Existence/status: HIGH.** This Soviet-era plant (commissioned 1960s-1970s) was listed at 105 MW in both the EVN 2011 Annual Report and the EVN 2017 Annual Report under GENCO 1. It is absent from the EVN 2018 Annual Report, which lists only Extensions 1 (300 MW) and 2 (330 MW) for GENCO 1 at Uông Bí, implying retirement between 2017 and 2018. PDP7 Annex 2 had planned retirement for 2021. Status recorded as Retired ~2017-2018 based on its disappearance from EVN's roster.

### NĐ Thái Bình II

**Existence/status: MEDIUM.** One of Vietnam's most delayed coal projects. Report 58 states: "Chậm tiến độ 3 năm và vẫn còn rủi ro chậm tiếp" (delayed 3 years with risk of further delay). Originally planned 2017-2018 per PDP7A, later reports estimated 2020-2021. Report 32 assessed: "Chưa xác định tiến độ hoàn thành" as of its date. PVN eventually completed both 600 MW units in 2022-2023 per industry press. It uses domestic coal (subcritical technology). Capacity 2×600 = 1,200 MW per both Report 32 and Report 58. Status is capped at MEDIUM because the COD is attested only by secondary trade press and not by an EVN or PVN annual report in the evidence pack.

### NĐ Vũng Áng II (BOT)

**Existence/status: HIGH.** The project "commenced construction in 2021, has a total investment of US$2.2 billion and comprises two units with a total capacity of over 1,200 MW." It "utilizes ultra-supercritical (USC) boiler technology – considered by experts to be the most advanced technology for coal-fired power plants in Vietnam." Unit 1, "with a designed capacity of approximately 600MW, officially commenced commercial operation at 0:00 on July 22, 2025." Unit 2 "is in the testing phase" and is "expected to be completed and put into commercial operation in the near future, aiming for the entire plant to generate electricity by the third quarter of 2025." Developer is VAPCO (Vung Ang II Thermal Power Company Limited), with Mitsubishi Corporation (40%) and Chugoku Electric Power Co. as principal shareholders. PDP8 Table 2 records 1,330 MW (slightly higher than 2×600 cited elsewhere). The capacity figure discrepancy (1,200 vs 1,330 MW) likely reflects nameplate vs gross rating; PDP8's 1,330 MW is used as the official planning capacity.

### NĐ Quảng Trạch I

**Existence/status: HIGH.** The plant "commenced construction in December 2021" and "comprises two generating units with a total installed capacity of 1,403 MW, utilizing supercritical fluid (USC) technology." The capacity of 1,403 MW from PDP8 Table 2 is higher than the 2×600 = 1,200 MW in earlier PDP7A documents, reflecting the actual turbine sizing. As of mid-2026, "The Quảng Trạch I thermal power plant is expected to connect its first unit to the national grid in April 2026 and begin commercial operation in May 2026." By February 2026, "the reverse power input for Unit 2 was successfully completed." Previously developed by PVN, transferred to EVN in October 2016 due to slow progress. EPC by CC1-Mitsubishi-Hyundai consortium. Note: sources alternate between describing the technology as "supercritical" and "USC"; treated as supercritical in the table pending clarification.

### NĐ Long Phú I

**Existence/status: LOW.** Long Phú-1 is "a proposed 'high efficiency' 1,200-MW coal-fired power station" by PVN. Construction was ~78% complete but suspended after the primary EPC contractor (Russia's Power Machines) was sanctioned by the US. "The proposed loan financing arrangements appeared to not be going ahead. As of March 2025, there was no further news on financing the project." Status is recorded as Construction (work paused) with confidence LOW for completion, as there is no clear path forward and the COD is highly uncertain.

### NĐ Quảng Trị I (coal BOT)

**Existence/status: LOW.** "In October 2022, the Thai Ministry of Energy announced that the project was cancelled following nearly a decade of delays." However, "in March 2025, the People's Committee of Quang Tri had a working session to discuss the revival of Quảng Trị-1. EVN stated that if they were the investor in the project, it would be developed using coal." "In June 2025, Quang Tri Provincial People's Committee proposed that MOIT formally request that EVN be assigned to the implementation of Quảng Trị-1." The project is in flux—previously cancelled, now being revived with potentially different fuel and developer. Status recorded as Announced (revived) with LOW confidence due to the uncertain investor, fuel choice, and regulatory approval.

### TBKHH Nhơn Trạch 3 & 4

**Existence/status: HIGH.** "On December 14, 2025, at Ong Keo Industrial Park, Dai Phuoc Commune, Dong Nai Province," the inauguration ceremony was held. "With a total designed capacity of 1,624 MW, the plants are expected to supply more than 9 billion kWh annually once operating stably." "The project is invested with cutting-edge technology, using GE's 9HA.02 gas turbines (USA)." "The plants achieve an efficiency of 62–64%, among the highest globally." Each unit is approximately 812 MW. The capacity split between NT3 and NT4 is based on the total 1,624 MW divided equally; exact per-unit nameplate not independently confirmed. Vietnam's first LNG-to-power project, supplied via Thị Vải LNG terminal (PV GAS).

### Ô Môn Power Center (Ô Môn I–IV)

Ô Môn is a power center in Cần Thơ with four planned phases. Ô Môn I is currently operating at 660 MW, listed under GENCO 2 as "Oil fired (FO)" in EVN 2018 AR. It was originally 330 MW per EVN 2011 AR, then expanded to 660 MW. PDP8 Table 5 plans to convert Ô Môn I to Lô B domestic gas. Ô Môn II (1,050 MW), III (1,050 MW), and IV (1,050 MW) are all planned CCGT plants using Lô B gas, but all are substantially delayed due to the Lô B gas pipeline development schedule. Report 58 notes Ô Môn III is "Chậm 5 năm" (5 years late) and Ô Môn IV is "Chậm 3 năm" (3 years late), both "đồng bộ tiến độ khí lô B" (synchronized with Lô B gas timeline). PDP8 Table 5 lists Ô Môn II at 1,050 MW (different from PDP7A's 750 MW), reflecting revised turbine specifications.

### LNG Bạc Liêu

**Status: MEDIUM.** PDP8 Table 1 lists LNG Bạc Liêu at 3,200 MW for the 2021-2030 period. The project is backed by Delta Offshore Energy (US). It has been in pre-feasibility stage for several years. At 3,200 MW, it would be one of Vietnam's largest single LNG projects. Progress has been slow, and the project's implementation timeline remains uncertain.

### NĐ Sông Hậu II and NĐ Vĩnh Tân III

Both are coal BOT projects listed in PDP8 Table 3 as projects facing financing and shareholder difficulties: Sông Hậu II at 2,120 MW and Vĩnh Tân III at 1,980 MW. The Revised PDP8 (April 2025) continues to list these among "3 projects/5,300 MW" (together with Nam Định I) that MOIT must negotiate with investors. "For 3 projects /5,300 MW (Nam Dinh I, Song Hau II, Vinh Tan 3)...facing difficulties in arranging capital and changing investor structure." Neither has started construction. For Vĩnh Tân III, CLP Holdings withdrew from coal in 2019. Both are effectively shelved pending resolution.

### Domestic gas projects (Cá Voi Xanh–dependent)

## Per-asset explanatory notes

### NĐ Uông Bí (original plant)

**Existence/status: HIGH.** This Soviet-era plant (commissioned 1960s-1970s) was listed at 105 MW in both the
EVN 2011 Annual Report
and the
EVN 2017 Annual Report under GENCO 1
. It is absent from the
EVN 2018 Annual Report

, which lists only Extensions 1 (300 MW) and 2 (330 MW) for GENCO 1 at Uông Bí, implying retirement between 2017 and 2018. PDP7 Annex 2 had planned retirement for 2021. Status recorded as Retired ~2017-2018 based on its disappearance from EVN's roster.

### NĐ Thái Bình II

**Existence/status: MEDIUM.** One of Vietnam's most delayed coal projects.
Report 58 states: "Chậm tiến độ 3 năm và vẫn còn rủi ro chậm tiếp" (delayed 3 years with risk of further delay).
Originally planned 2017-2018 per PDP7A, later reports estimated 2020-2021.
Report 32 assessed: "Chưa xác định tiến độ hoàn thành" as of its date.

PVN eventually completed both 600 MW units in 2022-2023 per industry press. It uses domestic coal (subcritical technology). Capacity 2×600 = 1,200 MW per both Report 32 and Report 58. Status is capped at MEDIUM because the COD is attested only by secondary trade press and not by an EVN or PVN annual report in the evidence pack.

### Ô Môn Power Center (Ô Môn I–IV)

Ô Môn is a power center in Cần Thơ with four planned phases.
Ô Môn I is currently operating at 660 MW, listed under GENCO 2 as "Oil fired (FO)" in EVN 2018 AR.
It was originally 330 MW per EVN 2011 AR, then expanded to 660 MW.
PDP8 Table 5 plans to convert Ô Môn I to Lô B domestic gas.
Ô Môn II (1,050 MW), III (1,050 MW), and IV (1,050 MW) are all planned CCGT plants using Lô B gas, but all are substantially delayed due to the Lô B gas pipeline development schedule.
Report 58 notes Ô Môn III is "Chậm 5 năm" (5 years late) and Ô Môn IV is "Chậm 3 năm" (3 years late), both "đồng bộ tiến độ khí lô B" (synchronized with Lô B gas timeline).

PDP8 Table 5 lists Ô Môn II at 1,050 MW (different from PDP7A's 750 MW), reflecting revised turbine specifications.

### LNG Bạc Liêu

**Status: MEDIUM.**
PDP8 Table 1 lists LNG Bạc Liêu at 3,200 MW for the 2021-2030 period.

The project is backed by Delta Offshore Energy (US). It has been in pre-feasibility stage for several years. At 3,200 MW, it would be one of Vietnam's largest single LNG projects. Progress has been slow, and the project's implementation timeline remains uncertain.

### NĐ Sông Hậu II and NĐ Vĩnh Tân III

Both are coal BOT projects listed in
PDP8 Table 3 as projects facing financing and shareholder difficulties: Sông Hậu II at 2,120 MW and Vĩnh Tân III at 1,980 MW.
The Revised PDP8 (April 2025) continues to list these among "3 projects/5,300 MW" (together with Nam Định I) that MOIT must negotiate with investors.

Neither has started construction. For Vĩnh Tân III, CLP Holdings withdrew from coal in 2019. Both are effectively shelved pending resolution.

### Domestic gas projects (Cá Voi Xanh–dependent)

The Dung Quất I-III and Miền Trung I-II CCGT projects (each 750 MW) are all dependent on the development of the Cá Voi Xanh (Blue Whale) offshore gas field by ExxonMobil.
PDP8 Table 5 confirms Dung Quất III uses "khí Cá Voi Xanh."

All five projects have been delayed in sync with the gas field's development timeline. The Revised PDP8 continues to include them for the 2021-2030 period.

*Aggregate statistics (for reference, not a separate table):* The inventory records approximately 85 thermal asset entries across all lifecycle stages. Operating coal-fired capacity totals roughly 25,000–26,000 MWe across ~30 plants/plant-groups, with an additional ~4,700 MWe under construction (Vũng Áng II at 1,330 MW now partially commissioned, Quảng Trạch I at 1,403 MW, An Khánh–Bắc Giang at 650 MW, Na Dương II at 110 MW, Long Phú I at 1,200 MW stalled). Operating gas-fired capacity (domestic gas) totals roughly 7,500–8,000 MWe across ~12 plants, with the newly commissioned Nhơn Trạch 3&4 LNG complex adding 1,624 MWe as Vietnam's first imported-LNG capacity. PDP8 and the Revised PDP8 plan approximately 22,000–24,000 MWe of new LNG-fired CCGT capacity and 10,000–15,000 MWe of new domestic-gas CCGT capacity through 2030-2035, though nearly all projects are at Announced or Pre-permit stage. Roughly 7,000+ MWe of planned coal capacity from PDP7/PDP7A has been cancelled or shelved in PDP8, reflecting Vietnam's shift away from new coal investment. These aggregates are approximate, reflecting the inherent uncertainty in planned-project capacities and the varying nameplate figures reported across sources.
